top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single credited writer) best meets the common criteria on the evidence available to me. His voice is distinctive: as publicly described, Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid turn memory, the body and dream into dense, recursive prose with formal ambition matched by structural control. The project appears to be one sustained authorship running from lyric poetry through the large novels, which fits the view that a whole authorship is judged, not one title. My main reservations remain open: his sentence-level achievement in Romanian is assessable only through translation and critical report; I cannot confirm which volumes beyond Blinding and Solenoid show sustained quality or whether the later novels extend rather than repeat the earlier project; and I am not sure the inward, maximalist mode carries breadth of significance. The poetry is thinly covered in translation, so the citation should rest on the prose with poetry only as its lyric root, and should make no lineage, completeness or lifetime's-work claim. These doubts apply to the evidence, not to a stronger rival, and the same translation limit applies to Adonis. No award (P000) is ranked second, because the case for P001 is solid enough that withholding the prize would be the worse outcome. Unanimity among the six files is not counted as merit.
